title: 東電・小林喜光会長退任　火中のくり拾い「人生最後、日本を強く」
extracted_text:
東京電力ホールディングス の小林喜光会長（79）が6月に退任する。「人生の最後を尽くす」との思いで2021年に就任し、柏崎刈羽原子力発電所（新潟県）の再稼働に奔走。東電再建に向けた数々の節目を先導してきた。

「赤紙がきたな」。小林氏は20年末ごろに会長就任の打診を受けた際の気持ちを振り返る。東電の会長ポストは当時、空席だった。同年の 日立製作所 出身の川村隆前会長退任後、政府や東電は複数の候補に打診したが、断られ続けていた。

東電は福島第1原発事故以降、廃炉や賠償費用の捻出で経営難が続く。東電の会長ポストについて、複数の財界関係者が「火中の栗を拾うようなもので、やりたがる人がほとんどいない」と口をそろえる。

ただ小林氏が「赤紙」と捉えたのはネガティブな意味ではなかった。国内最大の電力インフラ企業のトップを務めることは「日本社会のためだ」と考えたという。小林氏は就任当時75歳手前だった。

経営者としての最後の仕事になる――。そう覚悟し、公共性の高い東電で「社会のために最後を尽くそう」と決めた。

東電は4月30日、小林氏の後任に産業革新投資機構（JIC）の横尾敬介社長を内定したと発表した。

小林氏は同日、自ら退任にあたっての「思いを伝えたい」と退任記者会見を開いた。新旧トップがそろう記者会見も後日予定しているが、まずは異例となる退任者のみでの説明の場を設けた。

小林氏が思い入れのある事業として挙げた一つが柏崎刈羽原発の再稼働だ。

20年末に会長就任を受諾してから就任する21年6月までの間にテロ対策の不備が見つかった。「大変なことになった、というタイミングで、会長として迎えられた」。就任に先立つ記者会見では「安全の確保、信頼の回復を主導していくことが使命だ」と話した。

テロ対策不備により国から事実上の運転禁止命令が出た。ガバナンスやセキュリティー意識を抜本的に見直すことになった。

小林氏は「原発は二酸化炭素を排出せず、運転コストも低いため必要だ、という信念はずっと持っていた。安全を担保し、再び動かしたいという強い思いで執行とともに頑張ってきた」と話す。

「特に印象に残っているのは、地元との議論を4年間ずっと続けてきたことだ」とも振り返った。東電は25年2月に同原発6号機の再稼働への国の認可を取得し、同12月に地元同意を取り付けた。26年4月16日に約14年ぶりの営業運転を始めた。

小早川智明社長は4月30日の記者会見で「小林会長が培ってきた企業経営の経験や技術者としての見識を踏まえた叱咤（しった）激励が、どんなに心強かったか」と話した。

小林氏は三菱ケミカルホールディングス（当時）会長や経済同友会の代表幹事などを歴任した。歯に衣（きぬ）着せぬ発言が話題になることは度々あった。

ただ東電の現職幹部は「東電会長の在任中は誰かとぶつかることは避け、むしろ『調整型』の会長のように思えた」と明かす。

東電は政府や原発の立地地域などとの調整がひときわ多い。原発に対する批判が根強いほか、気づかうべき福島事故の被災者がいる。柏崎刈羽原発は立地自治体に電力を供給していない特異な環境にある。さらに東電は国から「借金」をして経営している。

小林氏は退任記者会見でも「国の資本が半分以上入るなかで、全体の最適解を求めつつ、心に改革の火をともし続ける難しさがある」と話した。「想像以上に政治と関わった」

小林氏の会長在任中、東電は福島第1原発の処理水の海洋放出やデブリ（溶融燃料）の試験的な取り出しなど、11年に発生した東日本大震災後の数々の節目を迎えた。処理水放出は海外からの批判も浴びた。対立を避ける「調整型」に徹し、東電が前に進むために避けて通れない決断を重ねた。

退任記者会見では「やり残したこともある」とも語った。「半導体が日本の最後の勝負であり、とりでになる。人工知能（AI）拡大など社会が急激に変化する。東電では柏崎刈羽原発の対応やデブリ取り出しに追われているだけになってしまった」という。

AIや半導体による電力需要の急増は世界の電力業界が抱える最大の課題となっている。日本にとっても産業発展のためには強靱（きょうじん）な電力インフラは欠かせない。

東電は資本提携による資金や知見の獲得によって、日本の産業基盤を強固にすることを目指す。小林氏が築いた東電再建への礎の上で、どのように資本提携の枠組みを構築するか。6月から横尾次期会長が率いる東電は早々に正念場を迎える。

「東電なら安心だ、この人なら信頼できる、といった心の価値の大切さを意識し、それぞれの日々の業務に取り組むことの大切さを説いてきた」。今後、資本提携で大きく形を変える可能性のある東電。小林氏の思いが変革への普遍的な基盤になる。

（中村信平）

translated_text:
Tokyo Electric Power Company Holdings Chairman Yoshimitsu Kobayashi (79) will step down in June. He assumed the position in 2021 with the determination to "devote the final years of his life," and worked tirelessly to restart the Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Nuclear Power Plant (in Niigata Prefecture). He has led TEPCO through numerous milestones in the company's reconstruction.

"The red notice arrived." Kobayashi recalled how he felt when asked to become chairman around the end of 2020. The TEPCO chairman position was vacant at the time. After the departure of Takashi Kawamura, the former chairman from Hitachi Seisakusho that same year, the government and TEPCO had approached multiple candidates, but all had declined.

Since the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant accident, TEPCO has continued to struggle financially due to the costs of decommissioning and compensation. Multiple business leaders agree that the TEPCO chairman position is "like picking up chestnuts from a fire" — hardly anyone wants to take it on.

However, Kobayashi's interpretation of the "red notice" was not negative. He believed that leading Japan's largest power infrastructure company would be "for the sake of Japanese society." He was about to turn 75 when he took the position.

His final work as a businessman — that was his resolution. He decided to "devote his final years to society" at TEPCO, a company with high public significance.

On April 30, TEPCO announced that it had selected JIC President Keisuke Yokoo as Kobayashi's successor.

On the same day, Kobayashi held a farewell press conference to share his thoughts. A press conference with both the old and new leadership was also scheduled for a later date, but this unusual setup provided an opportunity for the departing chairman to explain directly.

One of the projects Kobayashi was most passionate about was restarting the Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Nuclear Power Plant.

From the time he accepted the chairman position at the end of 2020 until he assumed it in June 2021, deficiencies in counter-terrorism measures were discovered. "It was a formidable situation, and I was able to welcome it as chairman." At his press conference before taking the position, he stated that "ensuring safety and restoring trust will be my mission."

Due to the counter-terrorism deficiencies, the government effectively issued an operating ban. There was a fundamental need to comprehensively review governance and security awareness.

Kobayashi said, "I have always believed that nuclear power is necessary because it doesn't emit carbon dioxide and has low operating costs. I have worked with the executive team with a strong desire to ensure safety and restart operations."

"What leaves the deepest impression is the four years of continuous dialogue with the local community," he also recalled. In February 2025, TEPCO obtained government approval to restart Unit 6 of the nuclear plant, and in December of the same year, secured local consent. Commercial operations began on April 16, 2026, after about 14 years.

President Tomoaki Kobayakawa said at the April 30 press conference, "Chairman Kobayashi's experience in corporate management and insights as an engineer, along with his encouragement and激励, were incredibly reassuring."

Kobayashi served as chairman of Mitsubishi Chemical Holdings (at the time) and as a representative director of the Japan Association of Corporate Executives. His blunt remarks were frequently discussed.


However, current TEPCO executives explained that "during his tenure as chairman, he avoided clashing with anyone, and came across more like a 'mediator' type chairman."

TEPCO requires significantly more coordination with the government and regions where nuclear plants are located. In addition to persistent criticism of nuclear power, there are the Fukushima accident victims to consider. The Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Nuclear Power Plant has a unique environment where it does not supply electricity to the local municipality. Furthermore, TEPCO operates by borrowing money from the government.

At his farewell press conference, Kobayashi said, "With over half of the capital coming from the state, there is difficulty in seeking optimal solutions for the whole while keeping the flame of reform burning in my heart." "I was involved with politics more than I expected."

During Kobayashi's tenure as chairman, TEPCO reached numerous milestones following the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake, including the海洋 release of treated water from Fukushima Daiichi and test removal of debris (melted fuel). The treated water release also drew criticism from abroad. He adhered to a "mediator" approach to avoid conflict, making unavoidable decisions to move TEPCO forward.

At his farewell press conference, he also mentioned "there are things left undone." "Semiconductors are Japan's last chance to be competitive. Artificial intelligence (AI) expansion means society is changing rapidly. At TEPCO, I've ended up just being occupied with responding to the Kashiwazaki-Kariwa nuclear plant and debris removal."

The rapid increase in electricity demand from AI and semiconductors is the biggest challenge facing the global power industry. For Japan, robust power infrastructure is essential for industrial development.

TEPCO aims to strengthen Japan's industrial base by acquiring funds and knowledge through capital partnerships. On the foundation of reconstruction that Kobayashi built, how will they structure the capital partnership framework? From June, TEPCO under incoming Chairman Yokoo will soon face a critical moment.

"I have emphasized the importance of the emotional value of trust — that 'TEPCO is reliable, this person is trustworthy' — and the importance of approaching each day's work with that in mind." TEPCO may undergo significant transformation through capital partnerships. Kobayashi's wishes will serve as a universal foundation for transformation.

(Nakamura Shinpei)
title_en: TEPCO Chairman Yoshimitsu Kobayashi Steps Down After 'Picking Up Chestnuts From the Fire' — 'Final Years to Make Japan Strong'
